clue.text: Greatly pleased — glowing, in fact!

definitions.meaning: read literally, the word describes something that has been lit and so is shining

explanation.surface: Someone is thrilled, positively radiant with joy.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is playful: the word can be read as 'lighted', so a thing that is literally glowing fits it as well as a happy person does.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone overjoyed is very pleased, and something set alight is shining, so both readings fit the one word.

clue.text: Protest over British disbandment

parts.note: a demo is a protest march or rally

explanation.surface: A protest is lodged against breaking up a British regiment.
explanation.walkthrough: DEMOB, short for demobilisation, is the British word for releasing troops from the forces after a war.
explanation.definitionFit: Demobilisation is the standing down of troops, the breaking up of military units.

clue.text: Glare? When upset, gods glare, OK?

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the following letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An angry glare: the gods are irritated and asking if that is all right.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram indicator 'When upset' rearranges GODS GLARE OK; the first 'Glare?' is the definition, with its question mark admitting the idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone a fierce, hostile stare is an idiom meaning to scowl at them.

clue.text: Gathered 24 grand first bestowed on man

indicators.note: first says the G comes at the front of the build
bestowed on places the meadow word on top of the man's name in this down entry

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand pounds
24 refers to the answer to 24 down, LEA, a meadow
Ned is a common man's name used in crosswords

explanation.surface: A gift of a thousand pounds is handed to a man first.
explanation.walkthrough: '24' is a cross-reference to another answer in the grid. In a down clue 'bestowed on' means placed on top of, and 'first' sends the grand to the very top.
explanation.definitionFit: To glean is to collect gradually, so gleaned means picked up or collected.

clue.text: Exactly as planned, former partner gets into series of races with omnibus

indicators.note: gets into means the ex-partner goes inside the letters for the races

parts.note: the TT, or Tourist Trophy, is the motorcycle race series on the Isle of Man
an ex is a former spouse or partner
an omnibus is a big book collecting several works

explanation.surface: A former partner joins a set of races, armed with a hefty anthology.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Omnibus' looks like a bus to ride but here means a collected volume.
explanation.definitionFit: A textbook example or move is a perfect model, done just as the manual says.

clue.text: Grown-up not at first admitting church to be soothing

indicators.note: admitting means letting the church abbreviation in among the other letters
not at first means the opening letter of the grown-up word is dropped

parts.note: a grown-up is an adult
CE stands for the Church of England

explanation.surface: An adult, hesitant at first, lets a church be a calming place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grown-up' looks like an adjective, but it stands for the noun; 'not at first' drops its opening letter and 'admitting' lets the church inside what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Dulcet tones are sweet and pleasant, gently calming to the ear.

clue.text: Giant has maiden very excited

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
agog means eagerly excited

explanation.surface: A huge figure has a young woman thrilled.
explanation.walkthrough: Gog and Magog are legendary giants of British folklore, whose effigies stand in London's Guildhall.
explanation.definitionFit: Magog is one of a pair of legendary giants in British and biblical lore.

clue.text: Medical man administers jabs for owls

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, an army doctor
pokes means prods or jabs

explanation.surface: A doctor gives injections to some owls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jabs' suggests injections from the doctor, but means prods. The mopoke is an Australasian owl named for its call.
explanation.definitionFit: The mopoke, or morepork, is a small owl of Australia and New Zealand.

clue.text: Sentimentality is not entirely desirable

indicators.note: not entirely means the word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: desirable things are good

explanation.surface: Being soppy is not altogether a good thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Goo is slang for mushy, cloying feeling, as in gooey romance.

clue.text: Kind of card expressing sorrow over closure of business

parts.note: in Scots, to greet is to weep, so greeting means crying

indicators.note: closure of picks the closing letter of the word business

explanation.surface: A sympathy card expresses regret at a firm shutting down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'expressing sorrow' points to the Scots verb 'greet', to weep, not to a condolence card.
explanation.definitionFit: A greetings card is the British name for a card sent for birthdays and occasions.

clue.text: Deer moving out of Scandinavia, eastwards at first

indicators.note: at first means taking the opening letter of each of the preceding words

explanation.surface: A deer migrates out of Scandinavia, heading east at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' applies to all five words before it: Moving Out Of Scandinavia Eastwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The moose is the largest member of the deer family, called an elk in Europe.

clue.text: Instrument unknowns cut down and sharpen

parts.note: x and y are the unknowns in algebra
to lop is to cut off or chop down
to hone a blade is to sharpen it

explanation.surface: An instrument for unknown purposes is cut and sharpened.
explanation.definitionFit: A xylophone is a percussion instrument of wooden bars struck with mallets.

clue.text: Amendment of a deft banker's bad sort of share transaction

indicators.note: an amendment changes something, so the letters that follow are rearranged

parts.note: the possessive is taken with its S as part of the letters

explanation.surface: A clever banker's poor deal on shares gets corrected.
explanation.walkthrough: In finance, bed and breakfasting is selling shares and buying them back the next morning, once used to lock in a tax loss or gain.
explanation.definitionFit: Bed-and-breakfasting is the trick of selling shares one evening and rebuying them next day for tax purposes.

clue.text: Something taken on spec provides a good soldier with sleep all right

parts.note: PI, short for pious, is crosswordese for good
a GI is an American soldier
a nap is a short sleep
oke is an informal form of OK, as in okey-doke

explanation.surface: A virtuous soldier is allowed a little doze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'provides' and 'with' simply link the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To buy something sight unseen, without inspection, is the idiom of buying an unseen purchase in a bag.

clue.text: Capital party in progress, a dance

parts.note: Riga is the capital of Latvia
a do is a party
on means happening, as in the game is on

explanation.surface: A party in a capital city is under way, with dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: The rigadoon is a lively old French dance in duple time.

clue.text: Superfine scent

definitions.meaning: excessively refined or fastidious, affectedly delicate

explanation.definitionFit: Chambers gives the word as an adjective for affectedly genteel, and as a noun it is a fragrant distillation of petals.

clue.text: Detail of unlimited cash given to board

indicators.note: unlimited means the outer letters of the word cash are removed

parts.note: a sign is a board, as on a shopfront

explanation.surface: A breakdown of the boundless money given to the directors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detail' looks like a noun but is the verb, as when a soldier is detailed for duty.
explanation.definitionFit: To detail someone is to allot them a task, which is to appoint or allocate them.

clue.text: Boy accepting bribes — one set up in control

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means the whole build is turned upwards, read from the bottom
accepting means the boy word takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: a lad is a boy
sops are bribes given to pacify someone
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A boy takes bribes, and one is caught in the act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns the whole of LA(SOPS I)D upwards. 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Having something at your disposal means having it under your command.

clue.text: "Goodbye", copper said

indicators.note: said means the letters are spoken out loud as a phrase

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A police officer says farewell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' suggests a policeman, but it is the metal; saying its symbol C U letter by letter gives the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A casual farewell meaning until we meet again.

clue.text: Native of America has work attracting very large amount of money

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work
OS is outsize, a clothing size
a sum is an amount of money

explanation.surface: An American has a job that brings in a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Native of America' sounds like a person, but is an animal native to the Americas.
explanation.definitionFit: The marsupial is native to the Americas, the only marsupial found in North America.

clue.text: Bruise — it could be made by a ruler

indicators.note: could be made by suggests the letters of the earlier words can be reshaped into a new form

explanation.surface: A bruise might be the result of a blow from a measuring stick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruler' looks like a straight edge that could raise a bruise, but is a Roman emperor.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiberius was the second Roman emperor, successor to Augustus.

clue.text: Volatile chap about to desert

indicators.note: about means the chap's name goes around the other word

parts.note: Eric is a man's name
to rat is to desert or betray

explanation.surface: A fickle man is about to run away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to' looks like 'on the point of', but 'about' is the container and 'to desert' is RAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something erratic is unpredictable and changeable, liable to swing suddenly.

clue.text: A singular honour to be had for this?

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
in card games the king is one of the honour cards

explanation.surface: A unique honour can be yours just by requesting it.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition completes the phrase 'to be had for the asking', meaning available on request; the question mark flags the indirect definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something free for the requesting is available simply by putting in a request.

clue.text: Wife set out, riding magnificent horse into town

indicators.note: out means the letters of the word set are thrown into disorder

parts.note: riding on means on
super means excellent, magnificent
a mare is a female horse

explanation.surface: A wife sets off, riding a splendid horse into town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges SET to EST. Weston-super-Mare is a seaside resort town in Somerset, England.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a seaside resort in Somerset in the West of England.

clue.text: Grip oddly adopted by the climbing crew

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means the letters are read upwards
adopted by means the odd letters are taken in by the word the
oddly picks the odd-numbered letters of the word grip

explanation.surface: A rowing crew takes up the stroke with an uneven grip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' gives GI from Grip; 'adopted by' puts it into THE as THGIE, and 'climbing' reads that upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A rowing eight is a boat crewed by eight oarsmen, so the number names the team.

clue.text: Spills that almost shattered vessels

indicators.note: shattered means broken into pieces, so the letters are rearranged
almost means the last letter of the word that is dropped

explanation.surface: Spills that nearly broke apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims THAT to THA; 'shattered' then rearranges SPILLS THA.
explanation.definitionFit: Tall ships are large traditional sailing vessels with high masts.

clue.text: Some arable area

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is taken, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: A portion of farmland.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'arabLE Area', and the whole clue also describes a meadow, a piece of open farmland.
explanation.definitionFit: A lea is a meadow or grassland, a stretch of open farmland.

clue.text: Beachwear, but useless

parts.note: tho is a short informal form of though, meaning but
NG stands for no good, meaning useless

explanation.surface: Swimwear that is nonetheless worthless.
explanation.walkthrough: THO, though, means 'but' as in 'nice, though pricey'.
explanation.definitionFit: A skimpy bikini bottom or a flip-flop sandal, both worn on the beach.

clue.text: S American money beginning to monopolise world

parts.note: the real is the currency of Brazil

indicators.note: beginning to picks the opening letter of the word monopolise

explanation.surface: Brazilian cash starts to dominate the globe.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm is a sphere or domain, as in the realm of science.

clue.text: Bird or its comb?

parts.note: in heraldry, or is the tincture gold
a comb is the fleshy crest on a bird's head

explanation.surface: A bird, or perhaps just the tuft on its head?
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' seems a joining word but is the heraldic term for gold; the question mark hints that the wordplay describes the bird's gold head stripe.
explanation.definitionFit: The goldcrest is a tiny European songbird with a golden stripe on its head.
